title: Missing Number
hints: The expected sum of `0...n` is known in closed form.
`x ^ x == 0` and `x ^ 0 == x` — XOR indices and values together.
jsBridge: Two classic tricks: the sum formula `n(n+1)/2 − sum`, and XOR of all indices and values. In Swift, the sum can overflow `Int` and trap, which is why XOR (or `&+`) matters more than in JS.

compass.q: In JS the sum formula silently loses precision past 2^53. In Swift it traps. Which failure mode is better?
Sum formula vs XOR vs `Set` difference: complexity and overflow risk of each?
Why does XOR work? What property makes `a ^ a == 0` useful here?
Finding gaps in sequence numbers (missed messages, dropped packets) is this problem.
